BroadcastChannel is same-origin only. A same-origin sender is already inside the page's trust boundary, and what it sends gets the same validation as any clipboard payload from another application. So the shared path adds no trust that the clipboard path lacks. The hook case 'a paste whose only type is the text the copy put there' constrains the fix. Without the share, readFromEvent finds nothing, the text '' places nothing, and run('clipboard.paste') never runs. The e2e emulation keeps only text/plain in setData, in all three projects, and covers both in-document and opened-later-tab pastes. findings.failure_scenario: Suppose the new cross-document test or the hook change fails on Firefox or WebKit, or on Windows (for example, the BroadcastChannel answer arrives after the paste under CI load). Main is then red for hours before anyone sees it. Meanwhile the held product stacks (M18.35 onward, which cp37 cleared to proceed) stack on top, and the red can no longer be attributed to one commit. The next driver, reading blockedReason, has no warning that ci is hours behind.

findings.summary: M18.205 recorded the iconify-pack-2198 baseline (32.799) as the median of five readings. Three of them (32.799, 33.803, 37.400) were taken on code before 84bdb8e, the faster pure SHA-256 the bench's encode hashes every file with. Only two (30.844, 31.053) are on the current code. The regression gate against current code therefore sits about 22% above its readings (37.719 / ~30.95), not the intended 15%. progress.md notes the later readings 'also include 84bdb8e', but neither the baseline nor the commit accounts for that.
findings.evidence: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 84bdb8e`: 797ff41 and 590e0a4 lack it; 60ce6af and 095be5d contain it. 84bdb8e changes packages/core/src/hash/sha256.ts. packages/core/src/shape/pack-encode.ts imports the core hash, and the bench times iconifyShapePack (format/bench/iconify-pack-2198.bench.ts: 'canonical JSON, hashing and validation of every file'). The readings are in progress.md (M18.243 entry). M18.243's row did require that 15% hold over all five readings, so the commit follows its row. The issue is the row's premise that all five measure the same code.
findings.failure_scenario: A later change makes the pack encode about 20% slower, for example 30.9 to 37 units. The nightly perf leg passes it as within tolerance against 32.799, so a real regression of the full-collection import goes unflagged until it passes 37.719.

findings.summary: ADR-0213 inserts a new source into the keyboard paste order (the newest shared copy, after the template and before images), and the editor now relies on a BroadcastChannel for cross-tab paste. ADR-0020 still lists a five-step keyboard order without that source and still says 'Cross-tab needs nothing extra' (line 142). ADR-0213's front matter does not say it amends ADR-0020, and ADR-0020 does not point to it. 04-rendering-and-editor.md was updated; the ADR that defines what a paste trusts was not.
findings.evidence: ADR-0020:106-112 lists the keyboard order 1-5. ADR-0020:142 says '**Cross-tab** needs nothing extra: tabs share the system clipboard'. `grep 0213 ADR-0020-clipboard-format.md` finds nothing. ADR-0213's front matter has only status, date and decision-makers.
findings.failure_scenario: A later change to paste (the M18 clipboard follow-ups, or an M7 or M11 regression fix) reads ADR-0020 as the contract and removes or reorders the shared-copy step, or skips its preconditions (no HTML, no file, exact text) as unspecified. The old-WebKit paste then breaks again with no ADR conflict to flag it.

findings.summary: The digest records c790660's review as a single 'r1 pass 0 findings' line. progress.md:4002 says r1 was changes-requested with four findings (F1 a StrictMode-closed channel that broke copy, F2 to F4) before a fix. That round was never recorded through review.mjs record, against code-review step 4 ('Record every round, including changes-requested'). As a result the pass is numbered r1 instead of r2.
findings.evidence: digest.log:1217: 'M18.242	8e3f48ee...	r1	pass	claude:general-purpose-subagent	0 findings'. c790660 adds only that one digest line. Rounds are computed by review.mjs (roundOf/nextRound), so a recorded changes-requested would have made the pass r2. Compare da60d79, which adds three lines (r1, r2, r3) for its three rounds.
findings.failure_scenario: The round cap (REVIEW_ROUND_CAP, the drive stop condition, M18.215) counts only recorded rounds. Unrecorded changes-requested rounds let a row pass its cap without the human allowance, and the audit trail loses the blocking defects the reviewer found, here a copy that threw before preventDefault under StrictMode.

questions.coherence: Coherent. The delta does what cp37 ordered: it reads the nightlies by leg, diagnoses the perf FAIL, records baselines from nightly readings, records the WebKit paste cause, then lands the fix. M18.250-252 split M18.233 for a real reason: a hand-written connectors.json would be an orphan to testShapePack. The split puts the contract change (ADR-0048 and ADR-0017 amendments) in one row and keeps M18.233 as an e2e closer.
questions.specFidelity: M18.249 meets its acceptance. M18.214's closure is carried by M18.214 itself. M18.243 records the cause with evidence: no bench code changed 797ff41..590e0a4, the CPU-bound benches in the same job read at or under baseline, and the spread was 11% within one run. M18.205 meets the amended route, except for F2. M18.242's fix meets the cp37 amendment's fix clause, including the unit case, and correctly stays todo. Its remaining work is the nightly evidence, :58, and F3. One risk for the nightly to settle: the specs copy unlabeled shapes, so the copy's text/plain is ''. If WebKit 26.5 does not replace the pasteboard with an empty string, the paste will carry the previous clipboard text, sameText will fail, and the counts will not rise. If the next nightly still shows 2/1 or 6/3, check this first.

questions.gateHonesty: m18-complete is 60/76 and cannot go green with 21 rows todo, no mutation evidence and no final review. The 521a424 baseline change carries a Threshold-change: trailer naming five runs. The tolerance and the ms limits are unchanged, so it is not a hidden weakening, but its effective headroom on current code is wider than stated (F2). check-tests-kept passes on every delta commit. Nothing was skipped or quarantined.
questions.architecture: Clean. clipboard-share.ts sits in the editor (DOM layer) with an injected channel and clock, and layering has 0 violations. The ADR-0213 trust model holds: a same-origin, size-bounded, shape-checked message still passes parsePayload before use, and nothing is persisted. Every-engine misfires (a plain-text clipboard equal to the copy's text, an emptied clipboard after a textless copy) are stated as consequences in the ADR.
